question: The sum of average variable cost and average fixed cost is known as ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**average cost**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The sum of average variable cost and average fixed cost is known as **average cost**.
 
• Average cost is the **total cost per unit of output**.
 
• It provides an idea of how much it costs to produce one unit of a good or service.
 
• Average cost is crucial for businesses to determine **pricing strategies** and profitability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Average Variable Cost (AVC)**

 
 
• AVC is the **variable cost per unit of output**.
 
• Variable costs vary with the level of output, such as raw materials, labor, and utilities.
 
• AVC is calculated by dividing total variable costs by the quantity of output produced.
 
• It helps businesses in understanding how variable costs change with production levels.
 
 
 
• **Average Fixed Cost (AFC)**
 
 
• AFC is the **fixed cost per unit of output**.
 
• Fixed costs remain constant regardless of the level of output, such as rent, salaries, and insurance.
 
• AFC is calculated by dividing total fixed costs by the quantity of output produced.
 
• As output increases, AFC decreases because the fixed cost is spread over more units.
 
 
 
• **Total Cost (TC)**
 
 
• TC is the sum of all costs incurred in the production of goods or services.
 
• It includes both fixed costs and variable costs.
 
• TC = Total Fixed Cost (TFC) + Total Variable Cost (TVC).
 
• Understanding TC is essential for budgeting and financial planning.
 
 
 
• **Marginal Cost (MC)**
 
 
• MC is the **additional cost incurred by producing one more unit of output**.
 
• It is calculated by the change in total cost divided by the change in quantity produced.
 
• MC helps businesses in decision-making regarding scaling up or down production.
 
• It is crucial for determining the optimal level of production where profit is maximized.
